clue.text: Parties a non-contributory member disrupts

indicators.note: to disrupt is to throw into disorder, so the letters of these words are scrambled

explanation.surface: A freeloader breaks up the gatherings he attends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disrupts' shuffles PARTIESA, the letters of 'Parties a'.
explanation.definitionFit: A parasite takes from its host and gives nothing back, a freeloading hanger-on.

clue.text: He knows how' to carry his liquor!

definitions.text: He knows how' to carry his liquor!

parts.words: He knows how' to carry his liquor!
parts.note: praise for a steady drinker, read literally as a man who carries loads and also shares his name with a dark beer

explanation.surface: Praise for a man who can hold his drink.
explanation.walkthrough: To carry one's liquor is to drink without showing it; here the man carries loads, and his name is also a dark beer.
explanation.definitionFit: A railway or hotel carrier of bags shares a name with a dark brown beer.

clue.text: The colour' can be erased

indicators.note: can be signals that the word erased can be made into something else by rearranging it

explanation.surface: A tint can be rubbed out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can be' reorders the letters of 'erased'.
explanation.definitionFit: Reseda is a greyish green, named after the mignonette plant.

clue.text: The traditionalist is back where he started

explanation.surface: The conservative fellow has ended up where he began.
explanation.definitionFit: A square is an old-fashioned, conventional person; back to the beginning is the phrase from a board game's first space.

clue.text: Be tricky to be helpful

parts.note: a card player who plays winning suit cards takes tricks, and the idiom means proving unexpectedly useful

explanation.surface: Advice to be crafty in order to help.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tricky' means taking tricks at cards with the winning suit.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to prove unexpectedly useful, from producing the winning suit in card games.

clue.text: The start of the Oaks

parts.note: reads like the off of a horse race, but means the nuts that oak trees grow from

explanation.surface: The horses are off at the start of a famous flat race.
explanation.walkthrough: The Oaks is a classic English horse race for fillies run at Epsom, so the surface suggests a starting gate; the trees in fact start from their nuts.
explanation.definitionFit: Every oak tree begins life as one of these nuts.

clue.text: Have a bite with the' best man

explanation.surface: Eat something with the groom's supporter at the wedding.
explanation.definitionFit: To munch noisily is to chomp; the top winner is a champion, shortened.

clue.text: It might be so daring as to warn the motorist

definitions.text: It might be so daring as to warn the motorist

indicators.note: might be says the letters of so daring could be turned into something else

explanation.surface: Something bold enough to caution drivers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'might be' reorders the letters of 'so daring'; the whole clue also describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A roadside notice exists to caution drivers about hazards ahead.

clue.text: Paper pattern

explanation.surface: A design for a dress cut from newsprint.
explanation.definitionFit: The Evening Standard is a London newspaper; a norm or model to follow is also called this.

clue.text: They deliver the' engineers' signals about the river

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, and the possessive adds an S

indicators.note: the signals go round, about, the abbreviation for river

parts.note: cues are signals to act
R is the standard abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: Army engineers send signals across a river.
explanation.walkthrough: The possessive in 'engineers'' supplies the S of RES. 'about' puts R inside CUES, giving CUERS.
explanation.definitionFit: To deliver someone from danger is to save them, which is what lifesavers do.

clue.text: Rubber substitute made back at a workroom ?

indicators.note: back means the word for a workroom is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: a lab, laboratory, is a scientific workroom
taken as written

explanation.surface: A rubber substitute is produced in a workshop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns LAB into BAL; 'made' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Balata is a latex from a tropical tree, used like gutta-percha in place of rubber, for golf balls and belting.

clue.text: Not in the first three in the realm of journalism

definitions.text: Not in the first three in the realm of journalism

parts.words: Not in the first three in the realm of journalism
parts.note: the realm's three traditional orders are clergy, nobles and commons; the press is counted as the next one

explanation.surface: Journalism has never ranked among the top three.
explanation.walkthrough: The three estates of the realm are Lords Spiritual, Lords Temporal and Commons; the press is called the next estate after them.
explanation.definitionFit: The press is known by this name as a power beside the three traditional orders of the realm.

clue.text: Where Samuel made a late appearance

definitions.text: Where Samuel made a late appearance

parts.words: Where Samuel made a late appearance
parts.note: a late appearance is one made after death: the Biblical witch's village where Saul had the dead prophet Samuel summoned

explanation.surface: Someone named Samuel turned up after time somewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'late' means dead: in 1 Samuel 28 the witch of this place calls up the ghost of the prophet Samuel for King Saul.
explanation.definitionFit: The witch of that village raised the dead prophet's spirit, so it is where he appeared after death.

clue.text: World organization quietly took an attitude, nem con

parts.note: UNO is the United Nations Organization
P is piano, the musical direction for quietly
to strike an attitude is to pose, so took one is posed

explanation.surface: A United Nations body softly adopted a stance with no one voting against.
explanation.walkthrough: Nem con is Latin shorthand for nemine contradicente, no one disagreeing.
explanation.definitionFit: A motion carried nem con had no voices raised against it.

clue.text: Shaw's play displays his wares

parts.note: Shaw's play Pygmalion is set among London street sellers; a seller of fruit from a barrow sets out his goods

explanation.surface: A Bernard Shaw drama shows off what the author has to sell.
explanation.walkthrough: Pygmalion opens in Covent Garden market among street traders; a barrow-boy there 'displays his wares'. The costermonger is the London fruit and vegetable seller.
explanation.definitionFit: A street hawker from a barrow is a seller who lays out goods for passers-by.

clue.text: Literary assemblies in transports !

explanation.surface: Collections of writing that send readers into raptures.
explanation.definitionFit: Collected volumes of an author's works and old public road vehicles share this name.

clue.text: There's just about one slip up in lattice making

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the whole run is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: re means about or concerning
I is the Roman numeral one
a lapse is a slip or error

explanation.surface: A small mistake in making a trellis.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns REILAPSE as a whole.
explanation.definitionFit: An espalier is a trellis or framework on which fruit trees are trained flat.

clue.text: What do you make of Aunt Sally ?

definitions.text: What do you make of Aunt Sally ?

parts.words: What do you make of Aunt Sally ?
parts.note: Aunt Sally is a fairground throwing game and anyone who is a target for criticism

explanation.surface: A question asking your opinion of a relative.
explanation.walkthrough: Aunt Sally is a British fairground game of throwing sticks at a dummy's head, and by extension anyone set up for attack.
explanation.definitionFit: A legitimate target for attack, like the figure at a fairground stall.

clue.text: Ploughing may be out of order in the City

definitions.text: Ploughing may be out of order in the City

parts.words: Ploughing may be out of order in the City
parts.note: ploughing drives a ploughshare through the soil; in the City of London aggressive selling of dubious stock is an improper practice

explanation.surface: Farming work would be out of place in the City of London.
explanation.walkthrough: A plough's blade is its share, so ploughing is pushing a share. The City is London's financial district, where hard-selling worthless shares is frowned upon.
explanation.definitionFit: Hard-selling doubtful stock to the public is an improper financial practice.

clue.text: No queues for the French cats' dance

indicators.note: queue is French for tail, so each word loses its last letter

parts.note: chat is French for cat, so two cats are chat chat

explanation.surface: The French cats perform a dance without lining up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'queue' means tail in French: CHAT CHAT with each final T removed.
explanation.definitionFit: A Latin American ballroom dance with a quick triple step.

clue.text: A wee cup of Scotch

parts.note: reads like a dram of whisky, but means a small cup in the Scots language

explanation.surface: A small glass of whisky.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of Scotch' means in the Scots tongue, not whisky.
explanation.definitionFit: In Scots dialect a small drinking cup or goblet.

clue.text: The letters are smaller in atmospheric diagrams

parts.note: air is the atmosphere, used here as an adjective
graphs are diagrams plotting data

explanation.surface: Weather charts come with tiny lettering.
explanation.walkthrough: In the Second World War, forces' letters were photographed onto microfilm and printed small to save weight in airmail.
explanation.definitionFit: Wartime airmail letters were reduced photographically, so the mail arrived as miniature prints.

clue.text: It's a way they have, right out East

parts.note: taken as written
E is the compass abbreviation for east

explanation.surface: People have their own habits, and a right turn goes eastward.
explanation.definitionFit: A road or path taken to get somewhere.

clue.text: Tea from Colombo he always prefers

indicators.note: the answer is taken out of the run of letters across these words

explanation.surface: A man in Sri Lanka's capital always likes tea best.
explanation.walkthrough: The OCR dropped 'he'; the scan prints it. The tea sits across 'ColomBO HE Always'; 'prefers' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Bohea is a black China tea, once a name for the best grade.

clue.text: Early airman came unstuck

parts.note: the Greek myth of the boy whose wax-bound wings melted when he flew too near the sun

explanation.surface: A pioneer aviator failed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'came unstuck' is literal: the wax holding his feathered wings melted, so he fell into the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Daedalus's son flew on wings fixed with wax, which melted near the sun.

clue.text: Searches to find the short answer among the shelves

indicators.note: among places the shortened word inside the word for shelves

parts.note: racks are frames of shelves
ANS is the short form of answer

explanation.surface: Someone looks through the shelves for the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To ransack a place is to search it thoroughly, turning everything over.

clue.text: Unusually severe 'officials

indicators.note: unusually means in an unusual way, so the letters are rearranged out of their normal order

explanation.surface: Some officials are strikingly harsh.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unusually' reorders the letters of 'severe'.
explanation.definitionFit: Reeves were local officials in Anglo-Saxon and medieval England, such as the shire-reeve or sheriff.

clue.text: Should this. be labelled " Wet Paint?

definitions.text: Should this. be labelled " Wet Paint?

parts.words: Should this. be labelled " Wet Paint?
parts.note: the warning sign on fresh paint, read as the title for a painting of the sea

explanation.surface: Is it time to put a warning notice on fresh paintwork?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wet Paint' is the notice on newly painted surfaces; read as a picture title it describes a marine view.
explanation.definitionFit: A marine painting depicts the sea, which is certainly wet.
